tier_reason: README Benchmarks section compares poplar maps against std::unordered_map (and 10 other maps) with g++ 7.3.0 -O3 on an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2; the driver code is public in kampersanda/dictionary_bench (bench executable, wrapper id 2 = std_unordered_map). Space numbers 0.24 vs 1.29 GiB and 1.09 vs 6.05 GiB, and the slower lookup/insert times, match the README tables.

corrections.caveats: Space win only, not a speed win: compact_bonsai_map lookup is about 2.9x-3.8x slower and insert about 3.4x-4.3x slower than std::unordered_map (derived from page data; .uk insert 2.87 vs 0.67 us/key). libstdc++ inferred from g++ on Linux (not stated). Benchmark driver is the separate repo kampersanda/dictionary_bench (README opened). Numbers are from 2018-2019 on an old Xeon. Method is peer-reviewed (Dynamic Path-decomposed Tries, ACM JEA 25(1), 2020). No deletion support.

notes: All metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 58 stars, not archived, last commit 2021-09-07 (abandoned). Kept as a memory-only entry against std::unordered_map.

tier_reason: README table shows CPEF 4.23 bits per posting vs PEF 5.15 (+17.86%) and BIC 4.60 (+8.04%) on the in-repo Gov2 sample; the method is peer-reviewed (Pibiri and Venturini, ACM TOIS 2017). Not A: the repo states gcc 5.4.1 and CMakeLists flags but no CPU model (the space metric does not depend on hardware anyway).

corrections.caveats: README numbers come from a 244-list Gov2 sample checked into test_data, not the full Gov2/ClueWeb09 of the paper. The TOIS 2017 paper was not opened (pages.di.unipi.it is blocked). Space win, not speed. Based on ds2i, with git submodules (FastPFor, stxxl, succinct) under their own licences. notes: The record said no licence, but the LICENSE file is an Apache-2.0 notice (Copyright 2017 Pibiri, Venturini), so usability becomes copyable. 14 stars, last commit 2018-06-04, abandoned. The tier rests on the peer-reviewed paper, which is real (search result) but was not opened.

tier_reason: The baseline comparisons exist only on the first-party project site gef.di.unipi.it (EGRESS_BLOCKED; only a WebSearch snippet was read). The repo's benchmark_results/benchs_st JSONs (Google Benchmark, bench_partition_size_tradeoff, 72-CPU 3.7 GHz host, release build) cover GEF variants only and contain no ALP/LeCo/DAC/Xz/Brotli rows. This is C on snippet evidence; drop to D if snippet-only numbers are not accepted.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (project site): up to 42.83% more compact than compressors with high throughput and random access (e.g. ALP, LeCo, DAC); compression ratios typical of general-purpose compressors (Brotli, Zstd) while keeping constant-time random access; up to 500x faster compression than general-purpose compressors (e.g. Brotli, Xz) and learned compressors (e.g. NeaTS); >1 GB/s throughput.
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from a WebSearch snippet of the project site gef.di.unipi.it (blocked, not opened); the README has no numbers. The repo has benchmarks/ (bench_compression, bench_decompression, bench_random_access, bench_multithread_scalability, bench_partition_size_tradeoff) and benchmark_results/ JSONs for GEF variants only, with no baseline rows, compiler or CPU model. Baselines are not SDSL or sux, so the entry is borderline for this category. Mostly a space win with random access. Needs C++20.

notes: The record's claim 'matches Xz and Brotli in space while orders of magnitude faster' was a loose paraphrase; it is replaced with the snippet wording. Apache-2.0, 4 stars, 136 commits, not archived, last commit 2026-02-01. A paper or the site would be needed for any tier above C.
